why: Count what one screen carries: 8 nav rows with 3 live counts, a 96px total over quota, a track with a pace tick, 6 supporting figures and a 7-row, 8-column table, all rescoped across 7 territories, and notice the order runs number, track, sentence, action so the screen gives a verdict before it shows data.

Notice the KPI cells are the chart tabs, and that one SVG holds a computed axis, three series told apart by weight and dash, a pace end tick, a crosshair with a dot per series and a tooltip, across 4 metrics and 3 compare modes of 37 daily points, with a table view and real gaps on days with no data.

Notice how a shared pace tick at 58% of the cell, with its header set exactly above it, replaces an axis, and that every total comes from the 37 POs in the file, so any row opens a modal whose rows sum to that number.

Notice 46 rows and 8 columns driven by 5 kinds of control, stage cards that show dollars and counts while acting as filters, a footer that restates the filtered count and total, and designed empty and undo states rather than a table that only looks full.

Notice how many states a control needs to feel real: 7 presets that stay in sync with any pick, typed fields that accept two date formats and only commit on Apply, and day cells with caps, band, hover preview, today tick and disabled states.
